lines: A class in a world now gets its world ready first: World loading, then Start riding.
The world downloads with its bytes counted, and stays on this device, so next time that step is done at once.
Then the renderer from main builds the shaders and warms up the first frames off screen, and Start riding takes focus.
If the download stops, the card says where, and Try again picks up from the bytes already received.
A browser without WebGPU or WebGL 2 rides the panorama: the plan, clock and bike work the same.
The class over its world, and the load card, from a phone to the full screen.
What the tests prove: the world downloads, resumes, is saved, and the ride waits for Start riding.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
